HIDDEN-001.name: NON_TRANSITIVE_EVIDENCE_BINDING_LADDER
HIDDEN-001.core: Evidence or validity at layer N may license/usefully support a test at N+1 but does not automatically establish the stronger semantic/role/outcome claim at N+1.
HIDDEN-001.STRONG_SUPPORT: The JSON explicitly represents at least two non-equivalent evidence/identity/role/result layers and encodes a rule, type distinction, required discriminator, or separate field preventing automatic promotion from the weaker to the stronger layer.
HIDDEN-001.WEAK_SUPPORT: The JSON structurally distinguishes layers that plausibly prevent collapse, but the non-transitivity rule is implicit rather than explicit.
HIDDEN-001.CONTRADICTION: The JSON explicitly states or operationalizes that satisfying a weaker identity/evidence layer is sufficient by itself to establish the stronger semantic/role/outcome layer without any additional premise.
HIDDEN-001.NOT_APPLICABLE: The JSON has no meaningful weaker-to-stronger evidence/binding relation; mere nesting, references, schema composition or required fields alone are insufficient.

HIDDEN-002.name: AMBIGUITY_IS_A_FIRST_CLASS_STATE
HIDDEN-002.core: When evidence does not discriminate a unique binding, unresolved/unknown/multiple candidates should remain representable until a discriminator arrives rather than being forced into a singleton.
HIDDEN-002.STRONG_SUPPORT: The JSON explicitly permits unknown/null/unspecified/multiple candidate states or optional unresolved fields and preserves them as distinct valid states until additional information is supplied.
HIDDEN-002.WEAK_SUPPORT: The JSON structurally permits omission/multiplicity/unknown-like values but does not explicitly connect them to insufficient discrimination.
HIDDEN-002.CONTRADICTION: The JSON explicitly forces exactly one semantic binding in a state that the same JSON identifies as underdetermined or unresolved, with no discriminator or declared default semantics.
HIDDEN-002.NOT_APPLICABLE: The JSON models a fully specified deterministic object or validation schema without an ambiguity/unknown/candidate-set question. Ordinary optional fields alone do not automatically count as support.

HIDDEN-003.name: FIRST_BREAK_LOCALIZATION_GENERALIZATION
HIDDEN-003.core: For an ordered prerequisite chain, the earliest unsatisfied boundary is informative and should remain distinguishable rather than being collapsed into one aggregate pass/fail or score.
HIDDEN-003.STRONG_SUPPORT: The JSON represents an ordered prerequisite/validation/provenance chain in which later admission depends on earlier stages and exposes per-stage/per-location failure or status information sufficient to localize where admissibility first breaks.
HIDDEN-003.WEAK_SUPPORT: The JSON has an ordered dependency chain and stage-specific state, but first-break localization is only implicit or incomplete.
HIDDEN-003.CONTRADICTION: The JSON explicitly declares an ordered prerequisite chain but intentionally collapses all stage failures into one aggregate status while discarding stage/location identity and asserts that nothing relevant is lost.
HIDDEN-003.NOT_APPLICABLE: Unordered arrays, nested JSON structure, schema composition, field requirements or chronology without prerequisite semantics do not count as a boundary chain.

promotion_rule.minimum_for_external_transport_candidate: At least two independently governed external repositories must provide STRONG_SUPPORT for a pattern, with zero direct CONTRADICTION, and support must survive a relation-destroying control appropriate to the represented structure.
promotion_rule.external_replication_requires: Independent implementation or analysis not authored/controlled by Hawkar-usls/JANUS; this rubric alone cannot establish external replication.
